pages.text: $(thing)Cigarette:$() craft exactly 1 loose tobacco with 1 Rolling Paper. Final quality is driven mainly by the tobacco's actual quality; cut choice is a preparation modifier. Manual crafting and Create assembly calculate the same score and preserve the same metadata.

For cigarettes, $(thing)Shag$() is ideal and Ribbon is a strong alternative. Rough and especially Flake reduce the final score, but leaf quality remains the dominant factor; a reasonable second-choice cut no longer turns excellent tobacco into a mediocre cigarette.
pages.title: Cigarette Cut

pages.text: $(thing)Cigar:$() combine 1 loose tobacco filler with 1 dry Tobacco Leaf wrapper. Final quality is $(item)75% filler + 25% wrapper$(), then adjusted modestly for filler preparation. Fermentation/aging already improve each component's leaf quality before this calculation.
pages.title: Cigar Recipe

pages.text: For cigars, $(thing)Rough$() is the ideal filler preparation and Ribbon is a strong second choice. Flake and Shag are less suitable. The wrapper's own quality now matters to the finished cigar. A cigar lasts $(item)100 puffs$(); a cigarette lasts $(item)15 puffs$().
pages.title: Cigar Cut & Puffs
